newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on export news, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on export news, soybeans.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on bearish input from the export sector, a drop in soybeans plus a technical setback, traders said.
"We started out lower on the weaker close yesterday and it's Friday so there was a lot of evening up," a trader said.

Wheat held relatively strong during the late selloff Thursday in the soybean pit but the wheat futures market early Friday failed to find aggressive new demand amid the sharp break in soybeans and the lower corn market.
Bearish export news circulated which included news The Philippines was backing away from the market.
Trade sources said the high prices of U.S. wheat also caused Algeria to pass on a tender for 75,000 tonnes of milling wheat and a South Korean firm passed on a tender.
Wheat remained underpinned by concerns about delays in the seeding of the U.S. spring wheat crop.

Residents of North Dakota's snowbound Red River Valley prepared on the first day of spring Thursday for what experts believe could be the worst flooding in a century. The Red River Valley is a key spring wheat growing region of the U.S.
Wheat closed one to 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with May down 7-1/2 at $3.90.
Technicians early Friday cited first support in the May at $3.92-1/2 a bushel and second support at $3.82-1/2. The session low for May was $3.87.
First resistance in the May was $3.94-1/2 and second resistance was at $4.04. The session high for May was $3.95-1/2.
The four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Friday.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) in the May closed at 61-1/2 percent. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.

Refco Inc and LFG Futures each sold two million bushels of July and FIMAT Futures sold 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said. Prudential Securities bought two million bushels of July and Merrill Lynch Futures bought one million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 19,000 contracts, below the 31,731 traded Thursday.

In wheat options, ING Derivatives bought 500 July $4.00 calls at 16-16-1/2 cents, Rosenthal Collins bought 200 July $4.20 calls at 11 cents, Paine Webber bought 200 July $3.70 puts and sold 200 July $3.40 puts at nine cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, below the 16,830 traded Thursday.
